description: Brazilian Portuguese terminology, dialect, and audit allowlist for the AlgaPSA pt locale.

domainTerms.notes: Use for user, MSP, or customer account concepts. Do not use European register variants.
Use compromisso for calendar appointments; use agendamento when emphasizing the scheduling action.
Use for approval workflows, timesheets, invoices, and request approvals.
Use ativo/ativos for managed devices, inventory, or configuration assets.
Use atribuição for assigning tickets, tasks, users, or technicians.
Use for workflow automation and automated operational behavior.
Use faturamento for the billing product area and invoice-generation process.
Use quadro for ticket boards, kanban boards, and workflow boards.
Use for prepaid or retainer hour pools. Keep bucket untranslated only in technical storage contexts.
Use orçamento only for project/financial budgets and spending limits. Never for sales quotes — those are cotações (see quote).
Use cliente for customer organizations and client-portal users.
Use portal do cliente for the customer-facing app.
Use for ticket, project, task, and document comments.
Brazilian spelling is contato. Do not use contacto.
Use for service contracts, contract templates, and contract lines.
Use for billable service lines associated with a contract.
Use for account credits, credit balances, and credit memos.
Use painel in prose. Dashboard may remain identical when used as a product/UI label in the allowlist.
Use alocação for technician dispatch (e.g. "Alocação de técnicos") and dispatch boards. Do not use despacho, which reads as a shipping/legal dispatch in Brazilian Portuguese.
Use for uploaded documents, folders, sharing, and document management.
Brazilian Portuguese commonly uses email without accent in product UI.
Use endereço de email for a single address field. For the plural section header (Email Addresses) use Emails or Endereços de email — native-reviewer suggestion 2026-07.
Use tipo de email for the label/type picker on an email row (mirrors tipo de telefone). Etiqueta de email is an acceptable alternative — native-reviewer suggestion 2026-07.
Use for platform/product extensions and installed extension metadata.
Use arquivo for files. Do not use ficheiro.
Use as noun for UI filters; use filtrar for the action.
Use ramo de atividade for the client/CRM industry field — native-reviewer confirmed 2026-07. Indústria reads as the manufacturing sector in Brazilian Portuguese, not a business vertical.
Use fatura for customer invoices in the product; avoid nota fiscal unless specifically referring to Brazilian tax documents.
Use faturamento for the invoice-generation area/process.

Use trabalho for the background-job entity (job name, job history, job details). Use execução only when the context is a specific run/execution of a job; keep execução reserved for the run/execution sense so it does not collide with the job entity. Never use correr/correndo/corrida for the running state — use "em execução".
Use for KB articles, categories, and review flows.
Use for software licensing and activation.
Use local for client or service locations; use localização for map/GPS contexts.
Use meta for project milestones (reviewer preference). Do not use marco.

Use Celular for the mobile phone-type label — native-reviewer confirmed 2026-07; Móvel is not used for phones in Brazil. Keep dispositivo móvel / dispositivos móveis for the mobile *device* category and aplicativo móvel for mobile apps.
Use for in-app and email notifications.

Keep onboarding as a loanword — it is standard and consolidated in the Brazilian MSP/IT market, and avoids the ambiguity of integração (which also means integration). Do not use integração/integração inicial for onboarding, nor literal embarque.
Use for invoice payments, online payments, and payment status.
Use funil de vendas para o pipeline comercial do CRM (confirmado pelo revisor nativo, alga0002243). Nunca gasoduto nem oleoduto: são dutos físicos.
Use Email principal for the primary email field on contacts/clients — native-reviewer suggestion 2026-07.
Use for ticket, task, and workflow priority labels.
Use progresso for progress labels and indicators (e.g. onboarding progress). The all-caps micro-label PROGRESS renders as PROGRESSO to match the sibling locales (es PROGRESO, it AVANZAMENTO).
Use for project management, phases, tasks, budgets, and project templates.

Use cotação (feminine: a cotação, cotações) for sales/service quotes — native-reviewer confirmed 2026-07. Never citação/citar (textual citation) and never orçamento, which is reserved for budgets (see budget).
Use for analytics, operational, billing, and audit reports.
Use for service requests, approval requests, and appointment requests.
Use agenda as a noun; use agendar/agendamento for the action or booking.
Use tela for UI screens. Do not use ecrã. Context nuance: use layout when referring to UI structure/design, and interface for a full system screen/interface.
Use for service catalog items, managed services, and support services.
Use for the billing/service catalog product area.
Use plural configurações for settings pages and controls.

Use Login único for the Single Sign-On feature name, tab labels, and titles; lowercase login único inside running text. Do not use Logon único — logon is a dated register for Brazilian product UI. Keep the abbreviation SSO untranslated (see identicalAllowlist).
Keep SLA as the standard abbreviation for service-level agreement.
Status is acceptable in Brazilian Portuguese and may remain identical.
Use pesquisa for satisfaction surveys and response analytics.
Tag is an accepted loanword in Brazilian software UI.
Use for project tasks, workflow tasks, and task inbox items.
Use for field/service technicians and technician assignment.
Keep tenant in developer/admin contexts; use organização only in user-facing prose when the customer organization is meant.

Keep ticket as a loanword — it is standard in the Brazilian MSP industry. ticket is masculine (o ticket, os tickets). Never use bilhete or ingresso, which imply an admission/travel ticket in Brazilian Portuguese.
Use lançamento de horas for billable time records; apontamento de horas is acceptable where space allows.

Use planilha de horas for grouped/submitted time entries and approval flows. Do not use folha de ponto, planilha de ponto, or quadro de horários — ponto implies attendance/clock-in, but this tracks billable hours.
Use usuário. Do not use utilizador.
Keep webhook as a technical loanword.
Use the noun Trabalho for the work phone-type label — native-reviewer confirmed 2026-07. Trabalhar is the verb "to work" and is wrong as a label; it stays valid inside sentences.
Use fluxo de trabalho in regular UI copy. Workflow can remain in integration names or technical labels when branded.

forbiddenTerms.reason: European Portuguese transport term; Brazilian Portuguese uses ônibus.
Wrong register for support tickets; bilhete means a pass/note. Use the loanword ticket.
European Portuguese phrase; Brazilian Portuguese uses banheiro.
Feminine of the mis-registered assignee term; use responsável.
Feminine plural of the mis-registered assignee term; use responsáveis.
Wrong register for a ticket/work assignee; cessionário is a legal/financial transferee. Brazilian PSA UI uses responsável (or atribuído a).
Plural of the mis-registered assignee term; use responsáveis.
Mis-registered quote noun; citar is the verb to cite. Sales quotes are cotações (native-reviewer confirmed).
Wrong register for a sales quote; citação means a textual citation or legal summons. Use cotação (native-reviewer confirmed).
Plural of the mis-registered quote term; use cotações.
European Portuguese transport term; Brazilian Portuguese uses trem.
False friend for a kanban/ticket board; conselho is a board of directors or advice. Reported by the native reviewer in alga0002243.
European spelling; Brazilian Portuguese uses contato.
Wrong register for a workflow run; corrida means a race/jog. Use execução.
Plural of the mis-registered run term; use execuções.
European Portuguese UI term; Brazilian Portuguese uses tela.
European Portuguese file term; Brazilian Portuguese uses arquivo.
A gas pipeline; the CRM sales pipeline is a funil de vendas. Reported by the native reviewer in alga0002243.
Wrong register for the client/CRM industry field; indústria reads as the manufacturing sector. Use ramo de atividade (native-reviewer confirmed).
Plural of the mis-registered industry term; use ramos de atividade.
Wrong register for support tickets; ingresso means admission ticket. Use the loanword ticket.
Dated register for sign-in in Brazilian product UI; use login (and Login único for the Single Sign-On feature).
An oil pipeline; the CRM sales pipeline is a funil de vendas.
Wrong register for a board (kanban/ticket board); placa means a plate/sign/circuit board. Use quadro. Allowlist legit hardware compounds (e.g. placa-mãe) only if asset hardware copy needs them.
Plural of the mis-registered board term; use quadros.
European Portuguese device term; Brazilian Portuguese uses mouse.
European spelling; Brazilian Portuguese uses registro.
European Portuguese phone term; Brazilian Portuguese uses celular.
European Portuguese user term; Brazilian Portuguese uses usuário.

dialectRules.rule: Prefer Brazilian product UI nouns: usuário, tela, arquivo, registro, celular, contato.
dialectRules.notes: These are audited through forbiddenTerms and targeted glossary checks.

dialectRules.rule: Keep the loanword ticket for support tickets (o ticket, os tickets).
dialectRules.notes: chamado is acceptable legacy wording, but ticket is now the standard term. Admission/travel meanings such as bilhete and ingresso are forbidden.

dialectRules.rule: Translate the sales-quote noun as cotação (feminine); orçamento is only ever a budget.
dialectRules.notes: Native-reviewer confirmed 2026-07. citação/citações/citar are audited through forbiddenTerms; watch gender agreement (cotação aceita, not aceito).

dialectRules.rule: Contact/phone type labels are nouns: Trabalho, Celular, Residencial — never verbs (Trabalhar) or European terms (Telemóvel); Móvel is reserved for devices (dispositivo móvel).
dialectRules.notes: Native-reviewer confirmed 2026-07 for the New Client page phone types.

dialectRules.rule: Translate invoice as fatura unless a Brazilian tax document is explicitly meant.
dialectRules.notes: Do not introduce nota fiscal into generic invoice UI copy.

dialectRules.rule: Keep common Brazilian software loanwords when they are standard or shorter than the literal alternative.
dialectRules.notes: Examples: email, status, tag, webhook, API, SLA, ticket, onboarding.

dialectRules.rule: Preserve every {{variable}} exactly as in the English source.
dialectRules.notes: Do not translate placeholders, braces, or variable names.

identicalAllowlist.notes: This allowlist is intentionally conservative; audit tooling should report identical English unless it matches one of these exact values, case-insensitive loanwords, or technical patterns.
